title: Oncall evacuation decision cards and scripting playbook
author: Priya Khatri
content:
Summary: This document provides concise decision cards and a scripted operator playbook for rapid evacuation of platform workloads (models, KV caches, and tenant traffic) when a region, availability zone, or GPU pool becomes unavailable or crossed into degraded state. It focuses on deterministic, observable steps that minimize customer impact while preserving cost and SLOs. Audience: - Platform operators and oncall engineers - Incident commanders and SRE leads - Platform product owners who approve runbook automation Preconditions (what must be true before following this playbook): - Incident declared with region or pool impact and severity >= Sev-2 - Primary telemetry observed: token-latency p99 > 2x target OR sustained error rate > 1% AND capacity credit consumption > 70% for 10 minutes - Access: operator role with "platform-ops" RBAC, access to allocator CLI and orchestration console, Slack incident channel created Quick glossary: - Evacuation: migrating active and queued requests away from an impacted allocator/pool/region to fallback targets with minimal token loss - Warmset: pre-warmed model instances that reduce cold-start latency for target region - Tenant slice: set of tenant IDs sharing the same priority and routing policy Decision cards (one-page actionable rules): 1) Severity: Regional split (Sev-1) - Immediate action: Initiate full-region evacuation orchestration. - Target: Move critical tenants and control-plane routes to primary fallback region within 6 minutes. - Fallback policy: Prefer Dedicated-compatible variants, then quantized cheaper variants if capacity constrained. - Communication: Page oncall pager team + notify sales-sent customer signals channel. 2) Severity: Pool degradation (Sev-2) - Immediate action: Soft-evacuation of high-latency slices; enable burst credits for business-critical tenants. - Target: Reduce p99 latency by 30% within 12 minutes or escalate to regional evacuation. - Fallback policy: Shift to warmset or lower-sequence-length kernel variant. 3) Severity: Model runtime misbehaving (Sev-3) - Immediate action: Swap to verified model variant (canary) for affected route; gate for quality regression. - Target: Maintain correctness SLI for templated prompts at 95% within 30 minutes. Operational playbook (operator steps) — follow exactly unless Incident Commander authorizes divergence: 1) Triage and declare: - Verify incident on status page and SLO dashboard. - Run: allocator status --region --pool

--format short and capture IDs. 2) Quarantine unhealthy pool(s): - Run: allocator set-eviction-policy --pool

--policy soft-evict --grace 90s - Note: soft-evict marks new work for routing away while letting in-flight requests drain. 3) Prioritize tenant slices: - Use tenant-scorecard to compute emergency-priority list. - Command: tenant-cli export-slice --policy emergency --output /tmp/slice.json 4) Execute staged migration: - Stage A (critical tenants): allocator migrate --from-pool

--to-region --slice /tmp/slice-critical.json --parallel 6 - Stage B (standard tenants): allocator migrate --from-pool

--to-region --slice /tmp/slice-standard.json --parallel 12 --defer-cold-starts true 5) Gate and validate: - Smoke checks: run smoke-checker --routes --max-p99 1.5s --min-success 95 - If smoke checks fail, rollback last migration batch and escalate to IC. 6) Stabilize and reclaim: - When p99 and error SLI within thresholds for 30m, mark old pool read-only: allocator set-readonly --pool
content2:
Scripting examples and snippets (operators should copy, edit, and paste where appropriate):

# Bash helper: evacuate-slice.sh (idempotent)
# Usage: ./evacuate-slice.sh <from_pool> <to_region> <slice-file> <parallelism>
set -euo pipefail
FROM_POOL=$1
TO_REGION=$2
SLICE_FILE=$3
PAR=$4

# stage a single migrant batch
allocator migrate --from-pool $FROM_POOL --to-region $TO_REGION --slice $SLICE_FILE --parallel $PAR --wait-for-batch || { echo "batch migration failed"; exit 2; }

# verification step
smoke-checker --routes /tmp/last-migrated-routes.json --max-p99 1.5s --min-success 95

# If smoke-checker fails, attempt 1 auto-retry then escalate

---

Post-evacuation validation checklist (table style rendered as bullet list for Slack copy):
- Validation: Token p99 for migrated tenants < target_p99 (target_p99 is route-specific)
- Validation: Error rate < 0.5% sustained for 30 minutes
- Validation: KV cache hit ratio recovered to within 10% of baseline
- Validation: Billing signals reconciled and tokens not double-billed
- Validation: Customer-facing routes marked green on synthetic canary dashboard

Rollback criteria (automated triggers):
- If migrated p99 > 2x target OR error rate > 2% for 5 minutes after migration, automatically reverse last batch: allocator migrate --reverse --batch <id>
- If total cost delta > 30% in first hour and customer impact not reduced, pause further migration and escalate to finance+IC

Operator guardrails and safeties:
- All migration commands require a minimal 2-operator confirmation (CLI prompt or Slack approval).
- Automated migrations are limited to a single operator approval in test regions only.
- Every migration is accompanied by a telemetry snapshot captured with: telemetry-snap --scope migration --path /tmp/mig-$(date +%s).json

Monitoring and dashboards to watch during evacuation:
- p99 token latency by route (Redwood Console > Observability > SLIs)
- Per-route error rate and 502/504 breakdowns
- Allocator capacity table: capacity-utilization, warmset-count, cold-start-rate
- Billing delta panel (real-time estimate vs baseline)
- KV cache staleness and rehydrate rate

Post-incident tasks (within 24h):
1) Run regression evals on representative prompt sets for every swapped model variant.
2) Reconcile cost and chargeback for emergency region usage.
3) Update warmset reservations if migration exposed capacity planning gaps.
4) Publish a short incident summary with annotated timeline and decision card deviations.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Runbook owner: Platform Incident Response (team) — primary: Priya Khatri, rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com
- Escalation: IC -> Platform SRE Lead -> Eng Director (contact chain on intranet)
- SLO targets to preserve during evacuation: overall system token p99 <= 1.5s (for paid tiers), error rate <= 1%

Change control and testing:
- Any changes to the automated migration script must be validated in the sacrificial region (staging-us-west-2) with synthetic stress tests and operator drills.
- Quarterly game-day: run a full evacuation exercise with at least one oncall in training mode.

Retrospective template (post-incident):
- Timeline (with UTC timestamps)
- Decision card used and any deviation justification
- Metrics before/during/after (p99, error rate, cost delta)
- What went well / what to improve (3 each)
- Action items with owners and due dates

References and related tools:
- allocator CLI docs: internal link to allocator runbook and flags
- tenant-scorecard: scoring rules and emergency-policy definition
- smoke-checker: synthetic canary runner and expected output format

Appendix A — Example escalation Slack template (copy/paste):
"Team: REGION-EVACUATION / Severity: Sev-1 / Affected: us-east-1 allocator-pool-34
Action: Initiated staged migration for critical tenants to us-west-2.
Status: Stage A migration in progress (6/12 batches). Smoke checks: PASS for first 2 batches, failing on batch 3. Investigating route X.
Request: IC to approve pause and manual verification.
Owners: platform-oncall, allocator-crew
Links: <SLO dashboard> <allocator audit log>"

Appendix B — Example simple smoke-checker JSON output (single-line for logs):
{"status":"PASS","p99":0.92,"error_rate":0.12,"routes_tested":12}
